- `openai/`:
  - `classify.rs` (393 lines): `chunk()`, `choice()`, `delta()`, `fragment()`, `legacy_call()`, `check_object()`.
  - `assembly.rs` (811 lines): `ChoiceAssembly` plus a `Check` shadow state. All checks run on a copy, then `commit`. `complete_arguments` requires function arguments to be `""` (shown as `{}`) or one complete JSON value.
  - `stream.rs` (903 lines): `OpenAiStream`. `rewrite_choice` and `notice_chunk` do the rewrite. `in_call` decides when array and delta rules apply.
  - `body.rs` (170 lines).
- `anthropic/`: `stream.rs` (876 lines, `AnthropicStream` with `BlockState`) and `body.rs` (96 lines).

**Classification.** `SMA-749 § 4.2`:
- OpenAI: a chunk is tool-free or tool-bearing by `choices[].delta.tool_calls` and `function_call`. Anything else is malformed. `{"error":…}` is an upstream-error record.
- Anthropic: dispatch on `data.type` (a differing `event:` name is malformed). `text`, `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` are tool-free. `tool_use` is tool-bearing. Any other block type is held as kind `Other` (fail closed).

**Assembly.**
- OpenAI, one `ChoiceAssembly` per choice. Tool data is accepted only for choice 0 at array position 0.
- Anthropic, one `BlockState` per content block. `partial_json` is concatenated, and the input is validated at `content_block_stop`.

**Rewrite** (`SMA-749 § 4.4`):
- OpenAI:
  - Remove the blocked entries from `delta.tool_calls` and renumber the rest from 0.
  - Never drop a frame or a choice entry (P-10).
  - Insert a notice chunk `{"delta":{"content":"[paigasus] tool call \"<name>\" was blocked (<code>)."}}` before the `finish_reason` frame.
  - `finish_reason` `tool_calls` becomes `stop` when no call remains.
- Anthropic:
  - A blocked `tool_use` becomes a `text` block at the same index (start, `text_delta`, stop).
  - `stop_reason` `tool_use` becomes `end_turn` when none remain.
- Non-stream: `BodyCalls::apply` re-serializes once. The notice is appended to `message.content`.
- Only frames that contain a blocked call are re-serialized (`Frame.payload` is re-emitted unchanged otherwise).

**"Unenforceable"** (`report.rs`):
- `ReportDecision::{Allow, Block, Unenforceable}`. `ReportEntry` serializes via `to_json()` (schema v1).
- Anthropic `server_tool_use`, `*_tool_result` and `mcp_tool_use` blocks are tool-free but reported `Unenforceable`, and are never decided. Emitted at `anthropic/stream.rs:~257` and `anthropic/body.rs:78`.
- Reports go in `: paigasus-decision {json}` SSE comments (`report_comment`) or the `paigasus-tool-decisions` header, capped at 2048 bytes (`header_value`).
- Tool names are sanitized to `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, with a 128-byte cap and a `name_sha256_8` hash.

**Usage extraction is NOT in CORE.** It is in the service (section 2).

## 2. Service crate (`SVC`)

**Hexagonal layout:**
- `domain/` is pure: `CallerContext`, `Credential`, `resolve_org`, and `limits.rs` (sliding window, budget periods, and the `LimitStore` port).
- `application/` holds `limits.rs` (`Limits::admit`) and `charge_guard.rs` (`ChargeGuard`).
- `adapters/` holds the transport and infrastructure code:
  - `http/` has `auth.rs`, `chat.rs`, `interception.rs`, `usage.rs`, `dto.rs`, `error.rs` and `bytes.rs`.
  - `iam/` has the `Iam` port (`#[async_trait] trait Iam`, `iam/client.rs:75`) and `IamClient`.
  - `limits/` has `memory.rs` and `redis.rs`, implementing `LimitStore`.
  - `openai/` has `OpenAiClient`, the egress adapter.

**Route registration** is in `adapters/http/mod.rs:107`. This is the only protected route; a `/v1/responses` route would join it:

`Router::new().route("/v1/chat/completions", post(chat::chat_completions)).route_layer(auth).route_layer(body_limit)`

- `auth` is `from_fn_with_state(AuthState{iam, dpop_enabled}, require_iam_auth)`.
- `body_limit` is `DefaultBodyLimit::max(max_request_bytes)`.
- `/healthz`, `/readyz` and the service-info route (which uses `require_authenticated` only) sit in other groups.
- The router also applies `http_metrics_layer("gateway")` and `CorrelationLayer`, then `.with_state(AppState)`.
- `AppState` fields: `iam: Arc<dyn Iam>`, `openai: Arc<OpenAiClient>`, `max_request_bytes`, `capabilities`, `limits: Option<Arc<Limits>>`, `dpop_enabled`, `tool_interception: Option<Arc<ToolInterception>>`.

**Handler flow** (`chat.rs:86`, `chat_completions`):
1. Extract `CallerContext`, which the auth middleware attached.
2. Parse a copy of the body into `ChatCompletionRequest{model, stream, messages, extra}` (`dto.rs`). The original bytes go upstream verbatim.
3. Refuse streaming if `capabilities.chat_stream` is off.
4. `state.limits.admit(&caller)` runs the rate limits and budget pre-check, returning a `ChargeGuard` or a 429. It runs only when `[limits]` is configured.
5. `guard.set_request_estimate(usage::request_tokens_estimate(&messages, body.len()))`, `set_ids`, `mark_sent`.
6. If interception is on, build `parse_request(Format::OpenAiChat, &body)` and a `DecisionContext`.
7. `state.openai.chat_completion(body, stream)` (`openai/client.rs:306`) POSTs to `{base_url}/v1/chat/completions`. It sets only the Bearer key, Content-Type and Accept headers, so the caller's headers never cross. It returns `ChatResponse::Full{status, body}` or `ChatResponse::Stream{status, stream: BoxStream<Result<Bytes>>}`.
   - Non-stream has a first-byte timeout. Stream has connect and idle timeouts only.
   - Dropping the stream cancels the upstream request.
8. Non-stream success: `usage::non_stream_usage(&body)` runs on the ORIGINAL body. It returns `Reported(usage.total_tokens)` or `Completion(estimate)`, and the result goes to `guard.set_reported` or `set_completion_estimate`. Then `interception::intercept_body` parses, decides and rewrites. A malformed body under `block` gives 502 `tool-interception-malformed-response`. The decisions go in the `paigasus-tool-decisions` header.
9. Stream success: with interception, `interception::intercepted_stream(stream, guard.take(), ti, ctx, turn, TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR)` is used. Without it, `terminal_sse_error_stream` is used.
10. Non-2xx upstream responses are forwarded verbatim, with `guard.mark_no_charge()`.

**Usage and billing:**
- `UsageScanner` (`usage.rs:84`) reads a COPY of the SSE bytes. It adds 1 token per data record, and the last `usage.total_tokens` wins. It is fed through `feed_scan` and `finish_scan` (`chat.rs:307` and `:317`) into `guard.set_stream_progress(records, reported)`. Usage appears in a stream only if the client sent `stream_options.include_usage`.
- The scanner reads `/usage/total_tokens` and `choices[]`. The Responses API puts usage at `response.usage` in the `response.completed` event, with `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `total_tokens`, so a new scanner or reader is needed (INFERRED from the shapes).
- `ChargeGuard::tokens()` returns the reported total, else request estimate plus completion estimate, capped at `MAX_TOKENS_PER_CHARGE`. The charge happens in `Drop`: `limits.store().charge(ticket, tokens, now)` and the `gateway_tokens_charged_total{source}` metric. So billing is settled when the response body is dropped or ends, in every path.
- `request_tokens_estimate` reads `messages[].content`. A Responses request has `input`, not `messages`, so this needs a variant.
- `dto.rs` requires `messages`, so a Responses DTO is needed too.
- `Limits::admit` takes only `&CallerContext`. The rate limit and budget are per principal and per org, and are not endpoint-specific. Some log strings and `"chat completion metered"` are chat-specific wording.

**Streaming relay** (`adapters/http/interception.rs`):
- The `Relay` unfold state owns the upstream, the `UsageScanner`, the guard, the `Interceptor`, a decide queue and one pending decision future (P-5), and a sleep timer.
- Loop: `feed_scan`, then `Interceptor::push`. On an upstream error: `finish_scan`, then `abort()`, which emits the terminal frame. On end: `finish_scan`, then `finish()`.
- `relay(format, …)` is generic over `Format`. `intercepted_stream` fixes it to OpenAI. Unit tests drive Anthropic through `relay`.
- The `Metric`-to-name mapping is `record(m)`.

**Config:** `[tool_interception]` is `ToolInterceptionConfig` in `config.rs`, with `enabled=false` default. `config.rs:40/49` doc comments say "on `/v1/chat/completions`". `OpenAiConfig{base_url, api_key (SecretString), extra_ca_bundle_path}` is at `config.rs:116`.

**SVC tests:** `tests/chat_proxy.rs`, `tool_interception.rs`, `limits_http.rs`, `openai_egress.rs`, `metrics.rs`, plus `tests/support/`.

## 3. Specs

**SMA-749** (`2026-11-09-sma-749-tool-call-assembler-design.md`, 577 lines)

Invariant I1 (§ 2, line 46), quoted:
> For every supported client parser P (§ 8.2), every tool call that P accumulates from the bytes the gateway emits was decided `Allow`, with the same choice, kind, name and arguments that the decider saw. Anything the gateway cannot classify with certainty is not forwarded (or triggers `on_failure`).

P1 and P2 (§ 8.1, lines 377-381):
> **Property P1 (I1).** For every generated upstream stream and every model M, every call M derives from the output equals a decision-`Allow` call by (choice, kind, name, arguments).
> **Property P2 (no panic, bounded memory).** The queue never exceeds `max_held_bytes` plus one record.

Non-goals (§ 2, lines 51-53), quoted:
> Tool calls encoded inside text content (ReAct / XML conventions, or a vLLM tool parser that fails and falls back to `content`); tools executed by the provider (Anthropic `server_tool_use`, `mcp_tool_use`); **the OpenAI Responses API**; request rewriting.

Related items:
- The header (line 12) also defers the policy decider (SMA-752), detectors (SMA-754), the decision log (SMA-755), the Anthropic ingress route (SMA-750) and MCP (SMA-756).
- D26 (line 84): only `/v1/chat/completions` is wired.
- Threat model: T1 model output is hostile. T2 the upstream may be non-conforming. T3 the caller is not an adversary.
- Acceptance criteria (§ 9): AC 4 requires P1 and P2 over at least 10 000 generated cases per format.
- § 11 holds implementation rulings (all fail closed): `choice_order`, `multi_choice_tool_calls`, the `object` rule, `type_shape_mismatch`, `incomplete_arguments`, `long_identifier`, `second_finish`, `block_interleave`, `lossy_number`, `preserve_order`, strict JSON scope (I-1), never drop frames (P-10), and 86 400 s caps.

**SMA-757** (`2026-11-14-sma-757-oracle-argument-prefix-design.md`, 418 lines)

The "client raise" and "no partial call" rule is D2 (§ 3) and § 4:
> D2: Oracle rule: **reject every strict partial.** At an excused raise, a call in the client's snapshot must match an allowed call exactly… This rule is decider-free, and it is what I1 says.

- § 4: "A snapshot at an excused raise is checked with the same rules as a complete run. The raise only excuses the fact that the client raised, and that it may hold fewer calls." `json_prefix` and the `partial` flag of `arguments_match` are deleted, and `check_i1` keeps `partial` only to excuse the raise.
- Why: SMA-752 policies will read arguments, so a prefix of allowed arguments can be a call the policy would deny.
- A raise is "excused" if `core_failed`, or if the client also raises on the upstream bytes.
- The new interceptor deviations (§ 5) are:
  - `fragment_after_bodyless_entry`
  - `chunk_without_choices`
  - `choice_without_delta`
  - a present `type` key counts as the type fragment (`repeated_type`)
  - `chunk_key` (H1)
  - `content_delta_type` (H2)
  - `array_outside_tool_calls`
  - `function_call_key`
- Real-traffic recordings (§ 2.4) were added as fixtures. Key finding: no real stream interleaves calls.
- The Responses API is explicitly deferred to SMA-769 (§ 9, line 404), quoted:
  > The OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`) is SMA-769, which starts after this change. It needs its own ingress, format and oracle models. It takes the D2 rule and the recording method of this spec from the start (§ 2.4).
- § 9 also says that `DATA_KEYS` in `json.rs` matches `input`, `input_schema` and `parameters` by key name only, so SMA-750 or SMA-752 must re-check it. A Responses `input` array may collide with this (INFERRED).
- § 2.4 notes that on `/v1/chat/completions`, gpt-6 models answer "Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported … use /v1/responses".

**Canonical rules and oracle models:**
- Canonical OpenAI form (§ 4.3):
  - tool-call indices appear in order 0, 1, 2, …
  - `id`, `type` and `name` each appear in exactly one fragment
  - `type` never changes, and `function` and `custom` never coexist
  - arguments are strings or null
  - arguments are complete JSON at completion
  - a legacy `function_call` and `tool_calls` never coexist
  - no fragment arrives after `finish_reason`
- Canonical Anthropic form (§ 4.3):
  - the block `index` equals the count of earlier starts
  - `tool_use.input` at start is `{}`
  - `message_start.message.content` is `[]`
  - no delta arrives for an unknown or stopped index
  - `partial_json` is a string
- Oracle models (all in `CORE/tests/support/oracle.rs`, 1281 lines). Each model reproduces its SDK's SSE decoder and accumulation, and runs to the end of the stream or to the point where the SDK raises (`Run{calls, error}`).
  - openai-python **3.40.0**: `_streaming.py` SSEDecoder, `_deltas.py accumulate_delta`, `lib/streaming/chat/_completions.py` (`run_openai_python`).
  - anthropic-python **2.3.0**: `_streaming.py` and `lib/streaming/_messages.py` (`run_anthropic_python`). It uses a jiter 0.19.0 partial-parse model (`Partial`, `partial_json`), measured 2026-11-14.
  - openai-node, `<not pinned: modelled only>`: `src/core/streaming.ts` and `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` (`run_openai_node`).
  - langchain-core and langchain-openai, `<not pinned: modelled only>`: `_merge.py merge_dicts`, `json.py parse_partial_json`, and `chat_models/base.py` (`run_langchain`). LangChain raises on any custom tool call.
  - The spec's first-party `chat-stream.ts` and `paigasus-sdk/chat.ts` parsers are covered by TS golden tests, not by Rust models.
- `check_i1(format, input, out, decided, core_failed)` runs the models per format through `runners(format)`. `OPENAI_RUNNERS` has 3 entries and `ANTHROPIC_RUNNERS` has 1.
- Quirks modelled: BOM, CR, trim, dispatch after `[DONE]`, duplicate keys, index handling, `content.delta` skipping, and `chunk.choices`.
- Real-SDK conformance (§ 8.2) checks golden files, not the Rust models. It uses `py/packages/paigasus-gateway-conformance/tests/test_golden_streams.py` (pinned openai and anthropic), `ts/packages/paigasus-sdk/tests/terminal-frame-golden.test.ts`, and `ts/apps/gateway-console/tests/unit/chat-stream-golden.test.ts`.

## 4. Tests in CORE/tests

- **`properties.rs` (131 lines):** proptest with `ProptestConfig::with_cases(10_000)`.
  - `openai_p1_and_p2_hold` and `anthropic_p1_and_p2_hold` draw `openai_scenario()` and `anthropic_scenario()`, render the bytes, apply random `cuts` (chunking), and run every decider.
  - `check_all_deciders` asserts that the stream finishes, that no `CANARY` appears under blocking deciders, that I1 holds through `check_i1`, and that `max_queued <= max_held_bytes + max_record_bytes` (P2).
  - Other proptests: observe mode (2000 cases), allow-all agreement (2000, restricted to framing quirks), and capitalised argument keys (1000).
- **`support/streams.rs` (634 lines):** grammar-based generators. A `Scenario` has choices, calls, `quirks: Vec<(Quirk, usize)>` and `cuts`. `Quirk` (OpenAI) and `AQuirk` (Anthropic) enums cover about 30 hostile shapes, including `DuplicateDelta`, `CaseFoldedKey`, `ProtoKey`, `Bom`, `AfterDone`, `Oversized`, `Interleave`, `NoChoicesKey`, `NoDelta` and `CapitalisedArgKeys`. Hidden calls are named `blocked_*` and carry `CANARY` in their arguments.
- **`support/driver.rs` (115 lines):** `drive(format, limits, chunks, decider)` runs the `Interceptor` synchronously and answers each `Decide` at once. It returns `Outcome{out, decided, max_queued, finished, metrics}`, with `core_failed()` true on any `RecordDropped` or `OnFailure` metric. `limits()` uses test limits (4096-byte records, 16 KiB held). `DECIDERS` = `block-by-name`, `block-all`, `allow-all`.
- **`oracle.rs` (126 lines):** tests of the oracle models themselves (SMA-757). The oracle is a proptest on `check_i1` with a raise record (P-M3, P-a, P-b, P-c) between two argument fragments: it asserts `Err`, and `Ok` when the raise comes after the last fragment. Also `partial_json` unit tests.
- **`fixtures.rs` (284 lines):**

## Sizing notes (INFERRED)

A Responses format is likely the size of the OpenAI plus Anthropic formats combined, since the work includes:
- a `Format` variant, a `Protocol` implementation, and body, request-turn and `UsageScanner` readers
- a `/v1/responses` handler plus DTO
- a new `OpenAiClient` method and a new oracle model with generators, fixtures and recordings

The service code is chat-specific in several places:
- `relay` and `intercepted_stream` take an `OpenAiByteStream` and `TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR`.
- `intercept_body` hardcodes `Format::OpenAiChat`.
- `OpenAiClient::chat_completion` hardcodes the URL.
- `request_tokens_estimate` reads `messages`.

All of these need parameterising by format.

The Anthropic ingress (SMA-750) has not been wired, so no existing handler shows how a non-OpenAI route plugs in. The only template is the chat handler, plus the `relay(format, …)` function that the tests drive with Anthropic.
